industry_scenarios.title: Parts and labour on one completed job

customer_asset.description: Fictional customer bicycle held for repair

steps: Create a job card and capture the reported issue.
Review the original estimate: three cables, two chains and four labour hours.
Customer approves; complete and invoice the work.
Link one returned chain to the credit note without refunding completed labour.
acceptance_checks: Parts reduce stock and record their cost; labour does not reduce stock.
The customer bicycle is custody property, excluded from owned inventory and business fixed assets.
Quote or job status alone does not post revenue.
Deposits, work in progress and warranty accounting need later review.

scenario.title: Keep customer property separate from workshop stock
scenario.goal: Follow parts, labour, customer-owned property and settlement examples without treating a job card as a posted module.
steps: Review the opening workshop stock and the separate customer-owned bicycle reference.
Trace a parts purchase and a labour/service sale through the ledger.
Review the customer receipt, supplier payment and returned part.
Confirm that customer-owned property does not enter the inventory valuation.
checks: Customer-owned property is excluded from stock balances and valuation.
The pack does not implement job cards, custody, scheduling or work-in-progress costing.
Parts and service income remain distinguishable in the teaching scenario.
